input: I think one cool project direction is common dev tools rewritten in rust.
follow_up_inputs: but also just common and niche tools.
task: Start the owner's new direction (dev tools in Rust, common and niche) with a measured first tool
errors: First jscpd timing used a pattern relative to the wrong root and matched nothing (0.7 s, no report); rerun with **/*.mjs.

/usr/bin/time is not installed in the container; timed with a /proc poller and then getrusage (tests/bench/rss.py). The poller under-reports peak memory for sub-second runs, so dupehound's memory figures come from getrusage only.
sibling-links: shipped the page with no sibling link (caught locally before CI); fixed in the second commit.
integrity_issues: Caught before commit: a draft of the candidates note said the usage.mjs copy reached 'about 994 ventures' (that was the number paired with one source file; the true figure is all 1,283 that ship one) and 'about forty' check_*.py scripts (28). Both corrected against the data.

doc_friction.issue: `record --model` writes a model id into a committed file; this session's harness forbids model identifiers in pushed artifacts, so the field was left null.
Tests used .wasm as the example of an extension nothing serves; adding the first WebAssembly asset broke three of them. Switched the example to .glb.

deviations.why: Copied the conventional usage.mjs although dupehound's own finding is that this file is the most-copied block in the repo; consolidating it is a separate change across ~1,283 ventures.
deviations.result: page and usage tests pass; noted in the blog post

notes: Local checks before push: cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy -D warnings (native and wasm32), cargo test (12, incl. brute-force cross-check run at 400 rounds once), node --test web/dupehound.test.mjs page.test.mjs usage.test.mjs (14 pass), node --test platform/pages/check.test.mjs (99 pass), validate_workflows.py, publish_surface.py --write, router validate, decision_queue --check, clauses.mjs dupehound, check_post_frontmatter, check_md_links. Page exercised in headless Chromium: example and a real folder pick, no console errors, only same-origin requests, no horizontal scroll at 375 px. After the first push: sibling-links-ci failed locally (dupehound was a crawlable orphan); paired it with npm-lockfile-duplicates-check both ways, with tests. readme_titles flagged the bare-slug README title; fixed. Ran check_md_links, check_code_refs, checklist_coverage, research/venture live links, readme_titles, conflict markers, prompts validate: all exit 0.
